pages.title: Submarines
pages.text:
[#](FFFFFF)[#]() **Key points**

- [#](FFFFFF)[#]() A sub floats until its **Ballast Tanks** fill with sea water. Pump in to sink, out to rise.
- The **Ballast Vent** is the sea valve and must touch the water.
- Each tank lifts about 75 units of ship mass.
- The **Onboard Computer** can hold a target depth for you.

**Create Deep Seas** adds submarines. A sub is a Create-style [#](2E5AAC)[contraption](entry://create_basics/contraptions)[#]() that moves as one solid, physical vessel, built on the same [#](7A3C9A)[Sable](entry://glossary/sub_level)[#]() and Aeronautics tech as [#](2E5AAC)[airships](entry://flight/airships)[#](). It dives by changing its own weight.

A submarine floats until its **Ballast Tanks** are filled with sea water.

- A **Ballast Vent** is the sea valve and must touch the water.
- Pipe vent, pump and tanks together.
- Pumping in makes the ship heavier and it sinks; pumping out lets it rise.

A Create pump pushes only the way its arrow points, whichever way its shaft spins, so a **Gearshift** does not reverse it.\
\
To switch between diving and rising, turn the pump round with a [#](2E5AAC)[Wrench](entry://create_basics/tools_wrench)[#](), or let an **Onboard Computer** run **Pump Controllers** for you.

Each empty tank lifts about **75 units of ship mass** (`ballastLiftPerTank` in the Deep Seas [#](7A3C9A)[config](entry://glossary/config)[#]()). A plank weighs about 1, an iron block about 3.5 and machines more, so a small iron sub can need a dozen tanks.\
\
Fit a few **spare tanks**: a sub with barely enough lift sinks slowly even with every tank empty.

With full tanks a sub drops fast: past 15 blocks a second in deep water, so start pumping out before the bottom.\
\
A sub resting on the sea floor may only lift off once its tanks are nearly empty. Give it a moment after the last tank drains.

pages.title: Ballast Tank
pages.text: Holds the water that weighs the ship down. Read its capacity with [#](2E5AAC)[Engineer's Goggles](entry://create_basics/tools_wrench)[#]().

pages.title: Ballast Vent
pages.text: The sea valve. At least one face must touch the sea. Every face takes a pipe.

The **Onboard Computer** can dive for you. Click its screen to set a target depth and speed, and it drives the pumps to hold that depth. **Pump Controllers** on the same ship are found automatically; pipe one between vent and tanks. Without a Computer a Pump Controller works like an ordinary pump. More controllers or faster rotation mean quicker dives.

pages.title: Onboard Computer
pages.text: Autopilot for depth. With a Sonar on board it can also follow the sea floor and keep the keel clear.

pages.title: Sonar
pages.text: Maps the floor, rocks, ships and mines around you on the Computer's screen.

Pumps and thrusters run on Create [#](2E5AAC)[rotation](entry://create_basics/rotation)[#]() and [#](2E5AAC)[fluids](entry://create_basics/fluids)[#](), so a sub is a Create machine through and through.\
\
[#](FFFFFF)[#]() **Tip:** press **W** over any Deep Seas block for its [#](2E5AAC)[Ponder](entry://start_here/tools)[#]().

pages.title: Submarine Propeller
pages.text: Strong in water, useless in air. Four in a 2x2 square facing one way merge into one big propeller.

pages.title: Water Thruster
pages.text: Uses water and rotation for thrust. More pressure and speed push you faster.

Hull strength, oxygen and airlocks are covered in [#](2E5AAC)[Hulls and Pressure](entry://ocean/hulls_and_pressure)[#](). Surface ships and sails are in [#](2E5AAC)[Sailing](entry://ocean/sailing)[#](). Where to dive: [#](2E5AAC)[Underwater Places](entry://ocean/underwater_places)[#]().
[#](FFFFFF)[#]() **In depth.** Deep Seas also holds an unfinished Create Abyss dimension, but it only switches on in development builds, so it is not in this pack.
